clue.text: Affected by bacteria, catching cold? One has doubts

indicators.note: catching means the first piece grabs and holds the second inside it

parts.note: a wound affected by bacteria is septic
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A germ-ridden person who has caught a chill is full of misgivings.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubter who questions accepted claims is a sceptic.

clue.text: Naughtily seduce about a hundred? Get on!

indicators.note: about means the scrambled letters go round the other piece
naughtily suggests misbehaviour, so the letters of seduce are mixed up

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to lure about a hundred people astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughtily' makes SUCEED from SEDUCE; 'about' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on in life is to prosper or do well.

clue.text: Get rid of king? No bother about that

indicators.note: about means the phrase for no bother goes round the letter for king

parts.note: ease means freedom from trouble or bother
R, from Latin rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off deposing a monarch as no trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase something is to wipe it out or delete it.

clue.text: Drinker serves up some bizarre potations

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
some means only part of these words is used, letters running across them

explanation.surface: A drunkard hands round some odd concoctions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes REPOT from bizarRE POTations; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A toper is a heavy habitual boozer.

clue.text: Aching terribly to restrict women's gossip

indicators.note: to restrict means to hem in, so the scrambled letters surround the other piece
terribly means badly, so the letters of aching are rearranged

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A painful ache stops women from chattering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' makes CHINAG from ACHING; 'to restrict' puts W inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinwag is an informal chat or natter.

clue.text: Dog, one of two stars

definitions.meaning: a gun dog breed that stands rigid indicating game
the two stars of the Plough that line up with the Pole Star

explanation.definitionFit: A gun dog breed shares its name with either of the two Plough stars that direct the eye towards Polaris.

clue.text: Pair tackling diminutive woman to get basket

indicators.note: tackling means taking hold of, so the two letters grip the name between them

parts.note: Annie is a pet form of the name Anne

explanation.surface: A couple wrestle a small woman to grab a hamper.
explanation.definitionFit: A pannier is a basket slung on a pack animal or bicycle.

clue.text: Merge bits of giant tree coming apart

indicators.note: coming apart means falling to pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fragments of a huge tree are splitting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bits of' just links, helping the picture of a tree in pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To integrate things is to combine them into one whole.

clue.text: Master perhaps wanting servant to provide part of book's content

parts.note: Master is an example of a title, as for a boy
a page is a boy servant

explanation.surface: A master who lacks a servant must write part of a book himself.
explanation.definitionFit: The title page is the leaf near the front giving a book's name and author.

clue.text: Letter I posted contains such a quick retort

indicators.note: contains means the answer sits within these printed words

explanation.surface: A letter someone mailed holds a sharp comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a swift, witty reply, from fencing's quick return thrust.

clue.text: Open a fizzy drink shortly, one to be imbibed

indicators.note: something imbibed is drunk down, so it goes inside the drink's letters
shortly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: champagne is the classic sparkling wine
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is told to uncork some bubbly and pour a glass to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims CHAMPAGNE to CHAMPAGN; 'to be imbibed' puts I inside it. 'Open' looks like a verb but is a noun: open countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Champaign is an old word for flat open countryside, a stretch of level field land.

clue.text: Add to set brought back

indicators.note: brought back means the word for set is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: An instruction to sum figures that have just been returned.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up is to add figures together into a total.

clue.text: What may be pencilled in here? It's hairy

definitions.text: What may be pencilled in here? It's hairy

parts.words: What may be pencilled in here? It's hairy
parts.note: pencilled in suggests a provisional diary booking, but it means drawn on the face with a make-up pencil, on a hairy strip above the eye

explanation.definitionFit: Make-up users darken the arch of hair above each eye with a cosmetic pencil.

clue.text: New singers making entrance

indicators.note: new signals the letters of singers are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Fresh choir members are making their debut on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is a formal word for going in, or a way in.

clue.text: Gun brought by the German impostor

parts.note: der is a German word for the
a ringer is someone fraudulently substituted, an impostor

explanation.surface: A firearm is supplied by a fraudster from Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A derringer is a small short-barrelled pocket pistol.

clue.text: Plant bill pulled up, bloomer getting untidy outside

indicators.note: outside means the jumbled letters wrap round the other piece
getting untidy means becoming messy, so the letters of bloomer are jumbled
in a down clue, pulled up means the letters read upwards

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A gardener pulls up a plant as a flower grows unkempt around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like a plant part or a bird's beak but is an account; 'bloomer' looks like a flower but is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocambole is a garlic-like allium, sometimes called sand leek.

clue.text: In winter men threatened going underground

indicators.note: in means the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Men menaced in winter take to the tunnels.
explanation.definitionFit: Interment is burial, placing a body in the earth.

clue.text: A piano coming in time for Christian celebration

indicators.note: coming in means these letters enter the word for time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A piano arrives just in time for a church festivity.
explanation.definitionFit: An agape was an early Christian love feast, a communal meal of fellowship.

clue.text: Ornament is very good on baby's bed

parts.note: pi, short for pious, is crossword slang for very good
a cot is a baby's bed

explanation.surface: A decoration looks very nice placed on the crib.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on' puts the first piece before the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A picot is a small decorative loop along the edge of lace or ribbon.

clue.text: Pathetic tie-up so badly arranged

indicators.note: badly arranged means the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A pathetically clumsy knot has been tied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Piteous means arousing pity, wretched.

clue.text: A symbol to encourage flagging Canadians?

definitions.text: A symbol to encourage flagging Canadians?

parts.words: A symbol to encourage flagging Canadians?
parts.note: flagging reads as tiring, but it means Canadians showing their flag, which bears a red emblem from a tree

explanation.definitionFit: Canada's national flag carries the red emblem of its native sugar tree.

clue.text: Part of Ireland with any number in formal gathering

indicators.note: in means the letter for a number goes inside the word for a gathering

parts.note: a muster is an assembly, as of troops
N stands for any number in algebra

explanation.surface: Lots of people turn up at an official assembly in an Irish province.
explanation.definitionFit: Munster is one of Ireland's four provinces, in the south-west.

clue.text: Quiet region in Spain is ideal

parts.note: P, for piano, means quiet in music
Aragon is a region of north-east Spain

explanation.surface: A peaceful Spanish region is perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a perfect model or example.

clue.text: Flood send the woman into torment

indicators.note: into means the pronoun is placed inside the word for torment

parts.note: to fret is to worry or torment
she refers to the woman

explanation.surface: A deluge drives a woman into anguish.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshet is a sudden rush of water, as from melting snow.

clue.text: Monkey in a tram going berserk

indicators.note: going berserk means running wild, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A monkey runs amok on board a streetcar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tamarin is a small South American monkey related to the marmoset.

clue.text: Say no emphatically, reversing malicious action

indicators.note: reversing means the whole run of letters is turned back to front

parts.note: say, as in for example, is EG
never is an emphatic way of saying no

explanation.surface: Someone flatly refuses, then backtracks out of spite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns EG + NEVER as one run, giving REVEN + GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenge is a spiteful act of retaliation for a wrong suffered.

clue.text: Words do have clout … And lots more!

definitions.text: Words do have clout … And lots more!

parts.words: Words do have clout … And lots more!
parts.note: reads as a saying about the power of language, but do, have and clout are all action words of one grammatical class, and there are many more

explanation.definitionFit: Doing words such as do, have and clout form the grammatical class of action words.

clue.text: Flair for grabbing ring — but marriage may become this!

indicators.note: for grabbing means the word for flair seizes the ring inside it

parts.note: a nose is a flair or instinct for something
O, the letter's round shape, represents a ring

explanation.surface: A talent for snatching a wedding ring is joked to lead to a married man's doom.
explanation.walkthrough: Old music-hall humour calls marriage the noose: a trap closing round a man's neck, so the definition is a playful image.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangman's loop is a jocular image for wedlock as a trap.

clue.text: Hole associated with region — this being depleted there?

definitions.text: Hole associated with region — this being depleted there?

parts.note: O, the shape of the letter, stands for a hole
a zone is a region or area

explanation.surface: The hole over a polar region is where the atmosphere's protective gas is thinning.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the famous hole over Antarctica is where this gas is being depleted.
explanation.definitionFit: The atmospheric layer of triatomic oxygen thins above the poles, forming the well-known hole.

clue.text: Hermit got troubled by an insect

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A recluse is upset by a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger moth is a striped, brightly coloured moth.

clue.text: Start of snow something forecast — Henry gets out jumper

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of the following word
gets out means the letter for Henry leaves the word

parts.note: the weather is what a forecaster predicts
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Snow is predicted, so Henry digs out a woolly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' is British for a knitted pullover.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumper is a knitted pullover, another word for a woolly top.

clue.text: Beginning to develop first sign of nerves before climb

indicators.note: first sign of picks only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: A climber feels the first flutter of nerves before going up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nascent is just coming into being, emerging.
